guidance: Planning aid for a course over the ground: it assumes a measured set and drift and ignores leeway, gusts, a stream that varies with time or place, and any tidal prediction, so check the heading against fixes and current charts before relying on it under way.
method: Ground velocity is the vector sum of the boat's velocity through the water and the current. The boat is steered on an unknown heading at a known speed through the water b, the current sets towards a known bearing with drift d, and the ground track must run along the requested bearing. In a frame rotated onto the track the current splits into an along-track component d cos(track - set) and a cross-track component d sin(set - track), positive to starboard. The water velocity that cancels the cross-track part is (-crossTrack, speed made good - alongTrack) and its length must equal b, so the speed made good solves s = alongTrack + sqrt(b^2 - crossTrack^2). The larger root is taken because the smaller one puts the boat stern-first down the track. The heading is then track + atan2(-crossTrack, s - alongTrack), normalised to 0 to 360, and the offset is that angle to port or starboard. Two insoluble cases are refused: a cross-track component wider than b, where the current is stronger across the track than the boat can claw back and no heading holds it, and s of zero or less, where the current runs dead against the track faster than the boat makes way. Bearings are accepted from 0 to 360 degrees true and normalised, so 360 reads as north; the boat speed is accepted from 0.1 to 60 knots and the drift from 0 to 10 knots. Bearings are reported to 0.1 degrees and speeds to 0.01 knots. Warnings fire when the offset reaches 30 degrees, when the speed made good falls below half the boat speed, and when the cross-track current reaches 80 percent of the boat speed. Leeway, a stream that varies with time or position, gusts and any tidal prediction are outside the model, so the heading assumes a set and drift measured from recent fixes.
